Materials

Choose the right material for your part.

PLA, PETG, ABS and TPU each behave differently. Some are best for clean models, others for functional parts, heat resistance or flexible protection. This guide helps you make a first choice – and we can recommend the final material after checking your use case.

Quick material finder
Clean visual modelBest for detailed indoor models and presentation parts.PLA
Functional everyday partA strong all-round choice for brackets, holders and housings.PETG
Technical part with higher heat exposureFor tougher parts, automotive accessories and post-processing.ABS
Flexible or shock-absorbing partFor dampers, seals, bumpers and soft protective parts.TPU

Material comparison at a glance

PLA

Mechanical behaviourVery stiff and hard, but brittle under overload.
Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 50–55 °C.
Best forPrecise indoor models, design parts and presentation objects.
Avoid whenAvoid for car interiors, direct sunlight, outdoor use or load-bearing parts.

PETG

Mechanical behaviourTough, impact-resistant and slightly flexible.
Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 70–75 °C.
Best forFunctional parts, brackets, housings and outdoor-related components.
Avoid whenAvoid when the cleanest possible surface or very easy support removal is the main priority.

ABS

Mechanical behaviourVery impact-resistant, tough, scratch-resistant and durable.
Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 85–90 °C.
Best forTechnical functional parts, automotive accessories, tools and replacement parts.
Avoid whenAvoid for large flat models, very fine details or outdoor use without post-processing.

TPU

Mechanical behaviourHighly flexible, rubber-like, tear-resistant and permanently elastic.
Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 60–70 °C and remains flexible at low temperatures.
Best forDampers, seals, protective covers, anti-slip feet and elastic connections.
Avoid whenAvoid when structural stiffness or clean overhangs are required.

PLA

Polylactide
Clean models & high detail

PLA is the best choice for clean visual models, precise prototypes and indoor presentation parts. It offers excellent surface quality and detail accuracy, but it is not suitable for heat, direct sun or mechanically demanding use.

Very stiff50–55 °C max.Best surface qualityIndoor use

Mechanical propertiesVery stiff and hard. Under overload, PLA tends to break rather than deform.

Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 50–55 °C. Not suitable for car interiors or direct sunlight.

AdvantagesExcellent surface quality, maximum detail accuracy and high dimensional stability.

DisadvantagesLow heat resistance and not weather-resistant. Best for indoor use only.

Printing restrictionsNo major restrictions. Overhangs, complex geometries and fine details can usually be printed very well. Supports are generally easy to remove.

ApplicationsDesign models, architecture models, form-check prototypes, accurate housings without load and decorative parts.

PETG

Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol
Durable all-round functional parts

PETG is a strong all-round material for functional parts. It combines stability with slight flexibility, is impact-resistant and works well for holders, brackets, housings and parts that may be exposed to moisture or outdoor conditions.

Tough70–75 °C max.Weather-resistantWater-repellent

Mechanical propertiesTough, impact-resistant and slightly flexible. Under overload, PETG tends to deform before it breaks.

Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 70–75 °C.

AdvantagesGood balance between stability and flexibility, weather-resistant, UV-resistant and water-repellent.

DisadvantagesSlightly glossy surface where imperfections may be more visible. More prone to scratches than PLA or ABS.

Printing restrictionsCan show slight stringing on the surface. Due to very strong layer adhesion, support structures can be harder to remove and may leave traces.

ApplicationsMechanical parts, brackets, workshop fixtures, outdoor housings, electronics boxes, holders and functional prototypes.

ABS

Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene
Tough technical parts

ABS is suitable for tougher technical parts that need higher mechanical strength, better heat resistance and good post-processing options. It is useful for automotive accessories, durable housings, tools and replacement parts.

Impact-resistant85–90 °C max.Post-processableTechnical parts

Mechanical propertiesVery impact-resistant, scratch-resistant, tough and suitable for long-term mechanical use.

Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 85–90 °C.

AdvantagesHigh thermal and mechanical resistance, good abrasion resistance and easy post-processing such as sanding or drilling.

DisadvantagesWithout post-treatment, ABS can be sensitive to UV exposure and may yellow outdoors.

Printing restrictionsABS shrinks strongly while cooling and can warp, especially with large, flat or massive parts. Fine filigree details are usually less precise than with PLA.

ApplicationsTechnical functional parts, automotive accessories, gears, heavily used tools, housings, covers and replacement parts.

TPU

Thermoplastic Polyurethane
Flexible protection & damping

TPU is a flexible, rubber-like material for parts that need to bend, absorb impact or protect other components. It is ideal for dampers, seals, protective covers, anti-slip feet and elastic connections.

Flexible60–70 °C max.Shock-absorbingOil-resistant

Mechanical propertiesHighly flexible, rubber-like, extremely tear-resistant and permanently elastic.

Temperature resistanceUp to approx. 60–70 °C. Remains flexible even at low temperatures.

AdvantagesExcellent shock absorption and damping. It does not break or splinter and has good resistance to oils and greases.

DisadvantagesNo structural stiffness. Not suitable for parts that need to hold a rigid shape under load.

Printing restrictionsOverhangs and unsupported bridges are difficult to print cleanly because the material is soft. Complex geometries that require support structures are often not practical, as the support can fuse with the part and may not be removable cleanly.

ApplicationsSeals, shock absorbers, protective covers, sleeves, anti-slip feet, elastic connections, flexible inserts and dampers.

Which material fits your use case?

Use caseRecommendedWhy
Architecture model / design modelPLAClean surface, high detail accuracy, indoor use.
Workshop fixture / functional holderPETG or ABSMore durable than PLA; choice depends on heat and load.
Automotive interior accessoryABS or PETG, sometimes TPUPLA should be avoided because car interiors can get too hot.
Outdoor housingPETGGood weather resistance, UV resistance and water-repellent behaviour.
Technical replacement partABS, PETG or TPUDepends on heat, mechanical load and flexibility.
Flexible seal / damping partTPUFlexible, shock-absorbing and tear-resistant.
Electronics housingPETG, ABS or PLADepends on heat exposure, rigidity and surface requirements.
Decorative partPLABest surface quality and detail accuracy.

How it works

From file to finished part.

A short, clear path. We don't ask for 20 settings up front.

Choose your path

Student, business or private. This sets the right pricing and options. Students see an instant package price; business and private orders get a tailored quote.

Upload your file, or describe your idea

Drop your STL, OBJ, 3MF or G-code file. No 3D file yet? Send a photo, sketch or reference and we'll create the model. Your upload stays private and confidential.

Choose material & colour

PLA, PETG, ABS or TPU, or pick "Not sure" and we'll recommend one. Then pick your colour.

Add an Expert Review (optional)

Most print problems start in the file. Add an Expert Review and we check geometry, wall thickness, dimensions and orientation before printing. Need more? File Editing & Optimization gives hands-on file repair. Included with the student Medium and Large packages.

We print in Düsseldorf

Your part is produced on our FDM machines in our Düsseldorf workshop, in the material, colour, speed and quantity you chose.

Receive your order

We ship across Europe, or you can collect your print at our Düsseldorf workshop.

Every upload is private and confidential, always. We never share or resell your models.

About us

The team behind 3Dnow

3Dnow is run by three people who have worked with 3D printing from every side: at university, inside a company, and at home for private projects. Those are exactly the three situations this platform is built for.

We also build the printers themselves. At iFactory3D we develop industrial belt printers for automated production, so we know both what the technology can do and where it gets complicated. And it does: demand for 3D-printed parts, products and ideas keeps growing, but slicing software, print settings and material choices still keep most people on the sidelines.

That's where 3Dnow comes in, and we kept the process short: you send us a model or an idea, tell us how you're ordering (student, business or private), and we print it. No printer to buy, no software to learn. You just get the finished part.

Martin Huber Additive Manufacturing Expert & Lecturer

Martin has worked with additive manufacturing long enough to teach it, which he does. As an industrial chemist he understands materials from the inside out, and he helped develop the belt printers the whole operation runs on. He's the one who can explain why something works, not just that it does.

Artur Steffen CEO & Entrepreneur

Artur turns the technology into something people can actually use. He's the entrepreneur of the team, thinking about how a student, a workshop and a hobbyist each need something different and how to make all of it simple. He runs the company and keeps it pointed at one goal: 3D printing without the learning curve.

Ben Schauf Additive Manufacturing Specialist

Ben makes sure a file actually becomes a print. He knows the machines, the materials and the countless small settings that decide whether a part comes out clean or warped. If your model has a weak spot, he'll catch it before the printer does.

FAQ

Answers before you upload.

The price depends on the estimated print weight, model volume, material, quantity and project type. Student orders use fixed packages based on estimated weight. Private and business orders are calculated according to the specific print requirements. This keeps pricing clear and based on the actual effort needed for your object.
You can choose the available materials and colours during the order process. We currently work with PLA, PETG, ABS and TPU. If you do not see the colour or material you need, contact us by WhatsApp or phone. We can check availability and order specific materials or colours for your project where possible.
Production time depends on the selected package, model size, material, printability and current production queue. Standard orders are printed in the order they arrive. We always try to provide a comfortable and fast service, but exact timing can only be confirmed after checking the file and order details.
The Expert Review is an important step before printing. It helps prevent failed prints, unusable parts and technical print problems. We look at mesh integrity, wall thickness, orientation and placement, overhangs, support surfaces, scale and units, intersecting geometry, shrinkage and tolerances where relevant. This helps detect problems before material and printing time are used.
Yes. We ship across Europe, including countries outside the EU where shipping is available. You can also pick up your order directly from our office in Düsseldorf.
Yes. Your uploaded files are treated as confidential. We do not share or resell your models.
If your model cannot be printed as uploaded, we will let you know. In many cases, the file can be adjusted through our File Editing & Optimization service. Our engineer can work directly with your file to repair, correct or prepare it for printing. If you do not have a file yet but only an idea, you can submit a request and we will check whether it can be turned into a printable model.
Yes. We are open to cooperation with universities, schools and lecturers. Contact us by phone or email to discuss student access, project support or a cooperation model.
